predecessors.name: Zagwe kingdom
predecessors.text: the Zagwe kingdom: Lasta, Tigray, the Eritrean highlands, Wag and Bete Amhara (the af-01-a hand-over)

successors.name: Italian Africa
successors.text: the whole empire, annexed by Italy on 9 May 1936 and merged into Italian East Africa on 1 June 1936

ledger.x: 1270: Yekuno Amlak ascends and founds the Solomonic line, replacing the Zagwe.
1299: Wedem Arad is at war with Ifat over eastern Shewa.
1316: Amda Seyon conquers Damot.
1316: Amda Seyon conquers the Muslim kingdom of Hadiya.
1316: Amda Seyon takes Gojjam.
1329: Amda Seyon campaigns in the northern provinces.
1332: Ifat is defeated and the eastern Shewa quarrel ends.
1332: Ifat becomes a vassal.
1332: Ethiopian rule crosses the Awash.
1403: Ifat's sultanate falls.
1403: Dawit I holds Ifat's land.
1415: the Walashma return and found Adal.
March 1529: Imam Ahmad's army defeats the Ethiopians at Shimbra Kure.
1531: Adal occupies Dawaro and Shewa.
1533: Adal occupies Bete Amhara and Lasta.
1535: Adal seizes Aksum and Tigray.
1536: Tigray is recovered.
21 February 1543: Imam Ahmad is killed at Wayna Daga and Adal leaves the highlands.
October 1544: Gelawdewos kills Abbas and recovers the south.
October 1544: the war ends in an Ethiopian victory ('Ethiopian-Portuguese victory').
1557: the Ottomans take the coast.
1572: the Oromo take Wej.
1593: Shewa and Damot are abandoned to the Oromo.
1607: Bale drops out of the tribute list.
1636: Fasilides founds Gondar as the permanent capital.
7 May 1769: Ras Mikael Sehul deposes Iyoas I and the Era of the Princes begins.
1855: Tewodros II rules from Debre Tabor.
11 February 1855: Kassa is crowned Tewodros II and the Zemene Mesafint ends.
1881: Yohannes IV rules from Mekelle.
1881: Ras Gobana Dacche makes Kaffa pay tribute.
1881: Jimma, Limmu, Gera and Guma become tributary.
ledger.cp: Gibe Oromo states (Jimma, Limmu, Gera, Guma)

ledger.x: 1886: the Arsi submit completely.
1886: Gobana Dacche occupies Wollega.
1887: Illubabor is incorporated.
6 January 1887: Menelik annexes Harar after Chelenqo.
1889: the Gurage region is annexed.
1889: Gobana Dacche annexes Hadiya territory ('Gobana Dacche annexed Hadiya territory').
1889: the capital is Addis Ababa.
1890: the northern highlands pass to the Italian colony.
1891: Bale, Sidamo, the Ogaden and Welayta are occupied.
1893: the Kambata are fully integrated ('Integration of the Kambata was completed').
1894: Gofa and Wollamo are taken and Mekonnen moves into the Ogaden.
1895: war with Italy begins ('1895-1896 (First Italo-Ethiopian War)').
January 1896: Aussa becomes a tributary of the Ethiopian Empire.
October 1896: Treaty of Addis Ababa.
1897: expeditions into Borana ('1896-1897 expeditions were launched into Borana').
1898: Beni Shangul is brought under control and the border with Sudan fixed ('Beni Shangul and the border with Sudan were controlled').
1898: Welde Giyorgis Aboye reaches Lake Rudolf (Turkana).
1898: Ras Tassama annexes Massonge and Gimirra.
1900: Kaffa is completely conquered.
1900: Kaffa is annexed (see the vassal_end; the year is a bridge).
1907: the southern border with British East Africa is first identified.
3 October 1935: Italy invades Ethiopia.
1 April 1936: Italy occupies the sultanate.
5 May 1936: Addis Ababa falls.
9 May 1936: Italy annexes Ethiopia.

wars.name: Amda Seyon's campaigns against Damot, Hadiya, Gojjam and Ifat
wars.outcome: Ethiopian victory: Damot, Hadiya and Gojjam conquered 1316, the northern provinces campaigned 1329, Ifat made a vassal 1332 and Ethiopian rule carried across the Awash into Dawaro and Bale.

wars.name: Ethiopian-Adal wars of Yeshaq I and Zara Yaqob
wars.outcome: No border change the pages name: Yeshaq I was killed fighting the Adalites in 1429 and Zara Yaqob defeated Sultan Badlay at Gomit in 1445.

wars.name: Ethiopian-Adal War
wars.outcome: Ethiopian-Portuguese victory; status quo ante bellum.

wars.name: Oromo expansion into the Ethiopian highlands
wars.outcome: The Oromo overran the empire's southern provinces and tributaries from the 1530s; the page dates Wej 1572, Shewa and Damot 1593, Bale's last tribute 1590-1607, Gojjam and Begemder raids about 1617, and the Wallo and Azebo overrunning Angot and parts of…

wars.name: Ethiopian-Ottoman conflict on the Red Sea coast
wars.outcome: The Ottomans held Massawa and the coast as Habesh Eyalet from 1557; Sarsa Dengel sacked Arqiqo in 1589, containing them on a narrow coastline strip.

wars.name: Funj-Ethiopian wars
wars.outcome: Frontier wars with no border change the page names: a full-fledged war in 1618-1619 and a Funj army on the Dinder River in March 1744.

wars.name: Zemene Mesafint civil wars
wars.outcome: Regional lords (Tigray, Yejju, Shewa, Gojjam, Simien, Begemder) fought for power until Tewodros II's coronation on 11 February 1855 (Battle of Derasge, 1855).

wars.name: British expedition to Abyssinia
wars.outcome: The British expedition succeeded; Tewodros II 'committed suicide rather than surrender'.

wars.name: Conquests of Menelik II
wars.outcome: Tribute from Kaffa and the Gibe states (1881); the Arsi (1886), Wollega (1886), Harar (6 January 1887), Illubabor (1887), the Gurage (1889), Bale, Sidamo, the Ogaden and Welayta (from 1891), Kambata (1893), Gofa and Wollamo (1894), Borana (1896-97), Beni…

wars.name: First Italo-Ethiopian War
wars.outcome: Ethiopian victory at Adwa on 1 March 1896; the Treaty of Addis Ababa (October 1896) delineated Eritrea's borders and Italy recognised Ethiopian independence.

wars.name: Ethiopian-Mahdist War
wars.outcome: Yohannes IV died in 1889 fighting the Mahdists (Ethiopian Empire page); the page gives no territorial change.

wars.name: Second Italo-Ethiopian War
wars.outcome: Italian victory: Addis Ababa fell on 5 May 1936, annexation 9 May, Italian East Africa formed on 1 June 1936; sovereignty restored 5 May 1941.

certainty.note: Highland provinces, Muslim marches and the southern tributaries have no surveyed frontier; the lines are approximate throughout, and in 1769-1855 the emperor's actual control was Gondar.
